intro: A rule is easier to believe after seeing it at work. These are things to open and study for ten minutes each: printed sheets, public screens and working tools. The product pages are vendors’ own descriptions. They are listed for how they arrange a screen, and nothing here vouches for their claims.

groups.title: On paper

items.title: Schedule for all sports disciplines
items.by: Michael Burke, in Otl Aicher’s department, Munich 1972
items.take: Dates, events and pictograms cross-indexed on one sheet, printed on both sides in seven colours.

items.title: Unigrid
items.by: Massimo Vignelli for the United States National Park Service, 1977
items.take: One sheet system behind the brochures of more than four hundred parks. The content varies and the structure holds.

items.title: World Geo-Graphic Atlas
items.take: Maps, sections, charts and symbols composed spread by spread. A landmark of layered, nested information graphics.

items.title: Isotype
items.by: Otto Neurath, Marie Reidemeister and Gerd Arntz, from 1925
items.take: A larger quantity is shown by more signs of the same size, never by a larger sign.

items.title: Sparklines
items.take: Word-sized graphics set beside the figures they explain, with a grey band where a normal range exists.

items.title: Feltron Annual Reports
items.take: Ten years of dense, precise personal data graphics. A study in typographic rigour at small sizes.

items.title: Visualizations for La Lettura
items.take: Compositions in layers, with a main structure and the secondary detail lightened behind it.

groups.note: Printed sheets that solved a dashboard’s problem before screens

groups.title: On screen

items.title: Is It Better to Rent or Buy?
items.by: Mike Bostock, Shan Carter and Archie Tse, The New York Times, 2014
items.take: Each slider sits on a small chart of the outcome across the whole range of that input.

items.title: Up and Down the Ladder of Abstraction
items.take: An interactive essay that moves between one concrete case and the whole range of a parameter.

items.title: Crossfilter
items.take: Three histograms of flight data. Brushing an interval on one filters the other two.

items.title: Ensemble meteograms
items.take: Several weather parameters stacked on one time axis, each drawn as box-and-whisker steps.

items.title: Public avalanche forecast
items.take: Danger ratings for three elevation bands over three days. A compact forecast matrix written for a wide public.

items.title: Weather, iOS 15
items.take: A page of rounded modules, each a small purpose-built instrument: a UV bar, a pressure dial, a wind compass.

items.title: Map of the Market
items.take: An early treemap on the web: nested sectors, area for size, colour for change.

items.title: Design an effective chart
items.take: Two clear talks on marks, axes, annotation and how charts work together as a system.

groups.note: Public screens that put a control, a spread or a stack of measures in the right place

groups.title: In working tools

items.title: Prediction Profiler
items.take: One small plot for each input, each a cross-section of the model’s response while the other inputs stay where they are.

items.title: Sensitivity Analyzer
items.take: Parameter sets, requirements and evaluated results side by side, with the details of a selected design beside the plot.

items.title: Analytical list page
items.take: A chart and its table in one view under a visual filter, for moving between the pattern and the exact rows.

items.title: Colour and layering
items.take: Surface roles as named tokens. In the light themes, layers alternate between white and a pale grey.

items.title: Temporary scenarios
items.take: Edits live inside a scenario and leave the underlying data untouched, with a summary of what changed.

items.title: Merchandise planning
items.take: A planning tool built around weekly open-to-buy, with scenarios and saved snapshots of a plan.

items.title: Scenario tools
items.by: Causal (now Lucanet) and Kinaxis, vendor descriptions
items.take: Causal let an input be a range and simulated the outcomes, and Kinaxis compares sandboxed scenarios side by side.

items.title: Design tokens format
items.take: The first stable, vendor-neutral token format, with theming and modern colour spaces.

groups.note: Listed for how they arrange a screen; vendors’ own descriptions, not endorsements
